data.name: Manmath
data.gender_notes: Manmath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manmath is the name of the Hindu god of love and desire. He is believed to control the emotions of love and infatuation. According to Hindu mythology, he is depicted as a god with a red face, carrying a bow and arrow, and surrounded by a cloud of intoxicating fragrance. The name Manmath carries the meaning “God of Love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manmath usually hope their child will grow to embody god of love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Manmath belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manmath total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Manmatha is mentioned as the god of love in the ancient Indian scripture, the Mahabharata. He is described as the king of serpents, and the husband of Rati, the goddess of love.
Manmatha is also mentioned in the Puranas, a set of ancient Indian texts. He is described as the god who controls desires and passions, and is responsible for instilling love between individuals.

He is often depicted as an attractive young man playing the flute, which is a symbol of love and desire. Manmath is seen on several modern platforms, including Hindu mythology, literature and poetry, and Bollywood movies. In Hindu mythology, Manmath is considered to be the god of love and desire, and is often invoked during weddings and other romantic occasions. In literature and poetry, Manmath is a recurring theme in love stories and poems, and is often used as a metaphor for the power and intensity of love. In Bollywood movies, Manmath is often depicted as a mischievous god who brings people together by stimulating their desires and helping them fall in love. These trends reflect the enduring appeal of Manmath as a symbol of love, desire, and the power of attraction.
